youtube.title: His Last Words Were "It's Not an Aircraft." Then He Vanished. | Frederick Valentich
youtube.description:
On 21 October 1978, 20-year-old pilot Frederick Valentich took off from Moorabbin, near Melbourne, in a Cessna 182 bound for King Island across the Bass Strait. Shortly after 7 pm he told Melbourne Flight Service that a large aircraft with four bright lights was near him; controllers said there was no known traffic at his level. He described it orbiting him, with a green light and a metallic appearance, and reported his engine rough idling. His final words: it was hovering, "and it's not an aircraft." Controllers then heard a metallic noise before contact was lost. A search of more than 1,000 square miles found nothing. Years later an engine cowl flap that may have come from his aircraft washed ashore on Flinders Island. The cause was never determined.

📂 Case File #028: The Valentich Disappearance

Sources: Wikipedia, "Disappearance of Frederick Valentich" and its citations (Department of Transport report); Snopes, "Frederick Valentich's 'UFO' Sighting and Disappearance".
